title: Unit – 3 : Session – 6 : SLO – 2  |  Stack Applications — Tower of Hanoi
sections: TOWER OF HANOI is a classic problem that demonstrates the use of recursion with stacks.
The minimum number of moves required to solve the Towers of Hanoi with n disks is 2^n - 1.
The recursive solution to Towers of Hanoi uses the STACK data structure to manage function calls.
In the Towers of Hanoi, disks are moved from the source rod to the DESTINATION rod using an auxiliary rod.
Each recursive call pushes a new STACK FRAME (activation record) onto the stack.
The Towers of Hanoi involves TWO recursive steps (move n-1 disks twice, plus one move).
The stack unwinds when the BASE case of the recursive function is reached.
The base condition in Towers of Hanoi is when ONE (n = 1) disk is to be moved.
Stacks in recursion help to TRACK (preserve) the order of operations in solving the puzzle.
The auxiliary rod in the Towers of Hanoi acts as a TEMPORARY STORAGE (buffer) during disk transfers.
